- Precision engineering capability and manufacturing of complex, low-to-medium-volume components across diverse materials (Aluminium, Titanium, Stainless Steel, Brass, Polycarbonates)

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Significant revenue fluctuations — Revenue swung from Rs 938.60 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 2,210.01 lakhs (FY25) to Rs 14,876.70 lakhs (FY26); variations may not indicate a consistent growth trend
- Customer concentration — Top five customers contributed 81.07% and top ten 92.06% of FY26 revenue from operations; loss of a key customer could materially hurt results
- Sector concentration in Defence — Defence alone accounted for 69.43% of FY26 revenue, making performance dependent on continued defence demand and approvals
- Export and foreign-exchange exposure — 27.47% of FY26 revenue derived from exports to 9 countries, exposing the Company to forex and international demand risk
- Short operating history — Company was incorporated only in 2021, giving limited track record for assessing performance
- Dependence on OEM customers and BTP/BTS approvals — Primarily supplies OEMs under build-to-print/build-to-spec models requiring customer approvals; loss of qualifications could disrupt orders

business.body: Millworks manufactures precision-engineered components and sub-assemblies used in regulated, mission-critical applications across aerospace, defence, railways and semiconductor machinery. It operates under Build-to-Print (BTP) and Build-to-Spec (BTS) engagement models, plus job-work arrangements, and primarily supplies Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs). In fiscal 2026 revenue from operations was Rs 14,876.70 lakhs, of which 27.47% was exports to customers in 9 countries.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Aerospace:** turbocharger components, fuel filter components / precision screens, turbine blades, nozzle components
- **Defence:** missile airframe components, guidance system housings, structural brackets and mounts, hydraulic cylinder parts, levelling and alignment components, drone structural frames, drone motor housings, BLDC motor stators, BLDC motor rotors, anti-drone system housings/brackets/support structures, drone sub-assembly assembly
- **Railways:** braking system components (air brake), train and metro door system components and actuators, train coupler components, pantograph system components
- **Semiconductor:** machine base frames, precision brackets and mounts, alignment plates, equipment housings, chip handling fixtures, load testing fixtures

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: The Company primarily supplies OEMs, Tier-1 and Tier-2 suppliers under Build-to-Print (BTP) and Build-to-Spec (BTS) engagement models, including full-scope manufacturing and job-work. Manufacturing is largely in-house across four Bengaluru units covering precision machining, sheet metal fabrication, sub-assembly and inspection. Surface treatment and finishing processes such as anodizing, passivation, electroless nickel plating and chemical blackening are outsourced to qualified external vendors under Company supervision, with material test certificates and process qualification records maintained. Forward participation in the drone ecosystem is pursued via a strategic investment of Rs. 5.75 crore in Quick Pay Private Limited (existing unsecured loan converted to equity), under which the Company manufactures and supplies drone components while Quick Pay handles integration, marketing and sale of finished drones. Big Bang Boom Solutions Private Limited is identified as a strategic supplier providing facility access, sub-assembly coordination and integration assistance for time-sensitive defence programs, including partial drone assembly at the partner's facility and 'Bill-to Ship-to' dispatch to customers.

concerns_observed: Extreme single-customer dependence on a related party: Quick Pay Private Limited (drone-based solutions) contributed 47.02% of total sales (Rs 6,992.76 lakhs) in FY2026, and the Company has itself invested Rs 5.75 crore in Quick Pay (an existing unsecured loan converted to equity) and shares common shareholders - so the largest revenue source is an affiliated counterparty rather than an arm's-length OEM.

The FY2026 revenue jump is a single-year, single-sector step-change, not a demonstrated trend: revenue rose ~6.7x year on year and the Defence sector alone leapt to 69.43% of FY2026 turnover from 6.81% in FY2025, while Railways (previously the mainstay at 68.20% in FY2025) fell to 23.65%.

Poor earnings-to-cash conversion: despite Rs 3,706.39 lakhs reported PAT, net cash from operations was NEGATIVE at (Rs 1,076.29 lakhs) in FY2026 (and negative in FY2025 at (Rs 291.89 lakhs)), driven by a Rs 12,893.84 lakhs increase in trade receivables.

Trade receivables of Rs 13,868.68 lakhs equalled 93.22% of FY2026 revenue and receivable days rose to 178 (from 72 and 50), locking almost an entire year of billings into working capital and creating heavy counterparty credit risk.

Dense related-party ecosystem centred on V3 Technologies (a partnership firm in which all four Promoters are partners) which is in a similar line of business (conflict of interest, mitigated only by a non-compete): FY2026 dealings include rent Rs 155.76 lakhs, purchases Rs 47.20 lakhs, advances given Rs 503.58 lakhs and a Rs 140.00 lakhs security deposit; Unit-1 and the registered office are leased from V3.

Concentrated supply side: the top-10 suppliers were 84.31% of purchases and the single largest supplier 44.05% in FY2026, all on purchase-order terms without long-term contracts; defence execution also depends on partner Big Bang Boom Solutions (facility access and part-assembly).

Pre-IPO capital actions favour Promoters shortly before the Offer: a 200:1 bonus issue on December 15, 2025 (1,25,08,200 shares - within the 18-month regulatory window) and a Promoter average cost of acquisition of about Rs 0.05 per share against a WACA of Rs 94.58 for the last-18-month primary issuances.

Extensive compliance history: non-compliances/compounding under Companies Act Section 10A (INC-20A), Section 185 (loans to directors), Schedule III, and FEMA/FCGPR filings, plus numerous late ROC filings and delayed GST/EPF/ESIC returns.

Working-capital-intensive model that will need external funding: the Company intends to deploy Rs 8,150.00 lakhs of Net Proceeds into incremental working capital for Fiscal 2027 (against a projected Rs 16,427.00 lakhs total requirement), on top of Rs 6,103.25 lakhs of machinery capex.

parameter_scores.basis: Revenue Rs 938.60 -> 2,210.01 -> 14,876.70 lakhs and PAT Rs 195.41 -> 524.90 -> 3,706.39 lakhs with EBITDA margin 29.55% -> 36.71%; absolute growth is exceptional but is a single-year step-change concentrated in one sector/customer, so durability is unproven.
FY2026 ROE 69.94%, ROCE 56.44%, RoNW 44.83%; very high but inflated by the one-year revenue surge on a small prior-year equity base (net worth Rs 232.98 lakhs in FY2024).
Total debt Rs 1,701.82 lakhs vs net worth Rs 8,266.99 lakhs (D/E ~0.21) at March 31, 2026; no promoter pledging; offset by only Rs 135.16 lakhs cash and Rs 7,223.36 lakhs trade payables.

Operating cash flow negative at (Rs 1,076.29 lakhs) in FY2026 and (Rs 291.89 lakhs) in FY2025 despite rising PAT; a Rs 12,893.84 lakhs receivables build means reported profit has not converted to cash.
Top-1 customer 47.02% (related party Quick Pay, Rs 6,992.76 lakhs) and top-10 customers 92.06% in FY2026; top-1 supplier 44.05% and top-10 84.31%; no long-term contracts on either side.
FY2026 revenue ~6.7x FY2025 with Defence surging to 69.43% from 6.81%; largest customer is an affiliated entity; receivables at 93.22% of revenue - quality of the earnings step-up is unestablished.

Wide V3 Technologies related-party dealings and shared premises; Section 10A / 185 / Schedule III / FCGPR non-compliances with compounding applications; late ROC/GST/EPF filings; 200:1 bonus within 18 months and promoter cost ~Rs 0.05/share; most directors lack listed-company experience.

100% of the Rs 6,103.25 lakhs machinery capex is unordered (only budgetary quotations); Rs 8,150.00 lakhs of proceeds go to working capital; issue size exceeds Rs 5,000 lakhs so a monitoring agency is required.

Floor Price and Cap Price are not stated in the extracted RHP text, so the offer P/E on FY2026 EPS of Rs 30.67 cannot be computed; DRHP peers Unimech (P/E 87.87) and Azad (P/E 96.45) sit at rich multiples on far lower RoNW.

red_flags: Largest customer is a related/affiliated party: Quick Pay Private Limited drove 47.02% of FY2026 sales (Rs 6,992.76 lakhs) while the Company holds a Rs 5.75 crore equity stake in it and the two share common shareholders.

Reported PAT of Rs 3,706.39 lakhs against NEGATIVE operating cash flow of (Rs 1,076.29 lakhs) in FY2026, with trade receivables at 93.22% of revenue (Rs 13,868.68 lakhs) - a material quality-of-earnings and cash-conversion concern.

200:1 bonus issue on December 15, 2025 (1,25,08,200 shares) within the 18-month regulatory window, combined with a Promoter average acquisition cost of about Rs 0.05 per share versus a Rs 94.58 WACA on recent primary issuances.

Company Law and regulatory non-compliances (Section 10A INC-20A, Section 185 loans to directors, Schedule III, FEMA/FCGPR) with compounding/adjudication applications pending, alongside numerous late ROC, GST, EPF and ESIC filings.

100% of the Rs 6,103.25 lakhs machinery capex funded from Net Proceeds is unordered as at the RHP date (budgetary quotations only), and the issue-size threshold triggers a mandatory monitoring agency.
Sudden single-year revenue and sector re-composition (revenue ~6.7x YoY; Defence 6.81% -> 69.43%; Railways 68.20% -> 23.65%), making the FY2026 base difficult to underwrite as sustainable.
strengths_observed: Rapid top-line and profit growth with high, expanding margins: revenue from operations rose from Rs 938.60 lakhs (FY2024) to Rs 2,210.01 lakhs (FY2025) to Rs 14,876.70 lakhs (FY2026); EBITDA margin expanded 29.55% -> 35.18% -> 36.71% and PAT grew Rs 195.41 lakhs -> Rs 524.90 lakhs -> Rs 3,706.39 lakhs (PAT margin 24.91% in FY2026), lifting EPS from Rs 1.94 to Rs 30.67.
Very high headline return ratios in FY2026: ROE 69.94%, ROCE 56.44% and RoNW 44.83%, on a net worth that grew from Rs 232.98 lakhs (FY2024) to Rs 8,266.99 lakhs (FY2026).
Low reported leverage: total debt of Rs 1,701.82 lakhs against net worth of Rs 8,266.99 lakhs (debt/equity ~0.21) as at March 31, 2026, and none of the Promoters' shares are pledged.

Precision-engineering play across four structurally supported end-markets - defence, railways, aerospace and semiconductor machinery - operating under Build-to-Print and Build-to-Spec models from four Bengaluru units, with AS9100D and ISO 9001:2015 accreditation and an export footprint of 27.47% of FY2026 revenue across 9 countries.

Rising machining capacity utilisation across units in FY2026 (Unit 1 74.46%, Unit 2 72.90%, Unit 3 75.67%, Unit 4-Machining 77.16%), indicating the existing asset base is being worked rather than idle.

Both DRHP-named listed peers (Unimech Aerospace at P/E 87.87 and Azad Engineering at P/E 96.45, FY2026) command premium multiples despite RoNW below 9%, so the aerospace/defence precision-components segment is valued richly by the market.
